classification.difficultyReason: Calculate a gradient from two explicitly supplied coordinates, then combine it with the given intercept in y=mx+c. These are routine linked procedures; no graph estimation, model selection or contextual interpretation is required.

content.prompt:
This scatter plot shows a linear relationship between English marks and History marks in a small class of students. A trend line passes through $(20,29)$ and $(70,49)$.

Find the equation of the line if the $y$-intercept is $21$.

spec.description: Ungridded scatterplot with black crosses, 10-unit ticks, 20-unit numeric labels, italic subject-axis titles and a blue trend line with two labelled points.
spec.mathematics: Horizontal variable x is English percentage; vertical variable y is History percentage. Trend line y=0.4x+21 passes through (20,29) and (70,49); line extent x=12 to x=75. Crosses are chosen scatter positions near the line.
spec.answerVisibility: The trend line and its two coordinate labels are student-visible givens. The equation is answer-only.
